issue_context.title: A bug in FileStream (async + buffer) since .Net 6?
comments:
@adamsitnik 

# CAUSE
This bug is caused by
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/dcda1e08cb8f421877388be2d685c009a31b1845/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/IO/Strategies/BufferedFileStreamStrategy.cs#L319-L324

And
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/dcda1e08cb8f421877388be2d685c009a31b1845/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/IO/Strategies/BufferedFileStreamStrategy.cs#L914-L935


# FIX
The fix is pretty easy. Just make the read buffer unavailable. Like what it does:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/dcda1e08cb8f421877388be2d685c009a31b1845/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/IO/Strategies/BufferedFileStreamStrategy.cs#L426-L439

e.g.  Add `_readLen = _readPos = 0;` and `write flush if need` before `return _strategy.ReadAsync(buffer, cancellationToken);` (Lines 319 to 324)

# QUESITON
But I don't understand the comment:
> To find out why we are bypassing cache here, please see WriteAsync comments.

Any idea?

@yeunglee big thanks for a very detailed bug report, I've sent a fix in #80432

> But I don't understand the comment:

The comment refers to the following comment, which explains why we have such perf optimization:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/7a6c31c107e4da7588f1dca65d4fbe65f52339f9/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/IO/Strategies/BufferedFileStreamStrategy.cs#L617-L630

> @yeunglee big thanks for a very detailed bug report, I've sent a fix in #80432
> 
> > But I don't understand the comment:
> 
> The comment refers to the following comment, which explains why we have such perf optimization:
> 
> https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/7a6c31c107e4da7588f1dca65d4fbe65f52339f9/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/IO/Strategies/BufferedFileStreamStrategy.cs#L617-L630

You're welcome. I posted a wrong comment. I have already deleted it.

review_comments: This is on the ReadAsync path. Is there any similar issue on the Read path? What about in BufferedStream? Just want to make sure we've audited all similar code paths that could have a similar issue.

> Is there any similar issue on the Read path?

There is not, and the test that I've added ensures this.

> What about in BufferedStream?

This particular optimization was not ported to `BufferedStream`. But I can add a `BufferedStream` test to be 100% sure.

> Just want to make sure we've audited all similar code paths that could have a similar issue.

Sure, that is a very good point. I've verified that neither Read or Write/WriteAsync suffer from same issue.
